title: Ezekiel Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 3.

questions.question: What was Ezekiel commanded to eat in Ezekiel 3?
questions.correctAnswer: A roll
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was commanded to eat a roll, as stated in Ezekiel 3:1: 'eat this roll, and go speak unto the house of Israel.'

questions.question: How did Ezekiel describe the taste of the roll he ate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sweet as honey
questions.explanation: Ezekiel said the roll was sweet as honey: 'and it was in my mouth as honey for sweetness.' (Ezekiel 3:3)

questions.question: To whom was Ezekiel sent to speak with God's words?
questions.correctAnswer: The house of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was sent to the house of Israel to speak God's words (Ezekiel 3:4): 'go, get thee unto the house of Israel, and speak with my words unto them.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 3, what kind of people was Ezekiel NOT sent to?
options: People of a strange speech and hard language
questions.correctAnswer: People of a strange speech and hard language
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was not sent to people of a strange speech and hard language (Ezekiel 3:5): 'For thou art not sent to a people of a strange speech and of an hard language, but to the house of Israel.'

questions.question: True or False: God said the house of Israel would hearken to Ezekiel's words.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: God said the house of Israel would not hearken to Ezekiel because they are impudent and hardhearted (Ezekiel 3:7).

questions.question: What did God make Ezekiel's face and forehead like?
options: Strong against their faces and harder than flint
questions.correctAnswer: Strong against their faces and harder than flint
questions.explanation: God made Ezekiel's face strong against their faces and his forehead as an adamant harder than flint (Ezekiel 3:8-9).

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel was to fear the rebellious house because of their looks.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: God instructed Ezekiel not to fear or be dismayed at their looks, though they are rebellious (Ezekiel 3:9).

questions.question: What did God tell Ezekiel to do with all His words spoken to him?
options: Receive in his heart and hear with his ears
questions.correctAnswer: Receive in his heart and hear with his ears
questions.explanation: God told Ezekiel to receive all His words in his heart and hear with his ears (Ezekiel 3:10).

questions.question: In Ezekiel 3, what does God compare Ezekiel's forehead to?
questions.correctAnswer: Adamant harder than flint
questions.explanation: God said He made Ezekiel's forehead as an adamant harder than flint (Ezekiel 3:9).

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel was sent to many people whose language he could not understand.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was not sent to many people of a strange speech and hard language whose words he could not understand (Ezekiel 3:6).

questions.question: Where did Ezekiel sit among the captives, according to Ezekiel 3?
questions.correctAnswer: Where they sat
questions.explanation: Ezekiel sat where the captives sat, remaining astonished among them for seven days (Ezekiel 3:15).

questions.question: What did the Spirit do to Ezekiel after he was told to speak to the captives?
questions.correctAnswer: Lifted him up
questions.explanation: The Spirit took Ezekiel up after he was told to speak to the captives (Ezekiel 3:12-14).

questions.question: True or False: God told Ezekiel he would open his mouth to speak when He commanded him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: God said when He spoke to Ezekiel, He would open his mouth to say the words (Ezekiel 3:27).

questions.question: In Ezekiel 3, what was the first command God gave Ezekiel?
questions.correctAnswer: Eat the roll
questions.explanation: The first command was for Ezekiel to eat the roll (Ezekiel 3:1).

questions.question: What instruction did God give Ezekiel after the hand of the LORD was upon him?
options: Arise and go into the plain
questions.correctAnswer: Arise and go into the plain
questions.explanation: God told Ezekiel to arise and go into the plain where He would talk with him (Ezekiel 3:22).

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 3:10, what is the instruction given to the 'Son of man' regarding God's words?
options: Receive them in your heart and hear with your ears
Write them on tablets of stone
questions.correctAnswer: Receive them in your heart and hear with your ears
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:10 instructs the 'Son of man' to receive all God's words in his heart and to hear them with his ears, emphasizing internal acceptance and understanding, as supported by Ezekiel 3:17 where he is told to hear the word at God's mouth.

questions.question: What task is Ezekiel given in Ezekiel 3:11 after receiving God's words?
options: To go to the captivity and speak to the children of his people
To build an altar for sacrifice
To write a scroll of lamentations
To gather the elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: To go to the captivity and speak to the children of his people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:11 commands him to go to those in captivity and declare God's messages, whether they will hear or refuse, which establishes his prophetic role (see also Ezekiel 3:17).

questions.question: What phenomenon does Ezekiel hear behind him as described in Ezekiel 3:12?
options: A voice of a great rushing praising the glory of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: A voice of a great rushing praising the glory of the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:12 describes hearing a great rushing voice behind him proclaiming 'Blessed be the glory of the LORD from his place,' indicating divine majesty and presence, complementing the spiritual lifting described in Ezekiel 3:14.

questions.question: How does the spirit affect Ezekiel in Ezekiel 3:14?
options: It lifts him up and takes him away, causing bitterness and heat of spirit
questions.correctAnswer: It lifts him up and takes him away, causing bitterness and heat of spirit
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:14 states that the spirit lifted and took him away, and he went in bitterness and heat of spirit, demonstrating the intense emotional and spiritual experience accompanying his prophetic mission, reinforced by the 'strong hand of the LORD' upon him.

questions.question: Where did Ezekiel go and what did he do among the captives according to Ezekiel 3:15?
options: He came to them at Telabib by the river Chebar, sat where they sat, and remained astonished for seven days
He built a tent and taught them the law
He led them in a prayer for deliverance
He immediately began prophesying to them
questions.correctAnswer: He came to them at Telabib by the river Chebar, sat where they sat, and remained astonished for seven days
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:15 describes his arrival at Telabib among the captives where he sat with them and was astonished for seven days, indicating a period of reflection and solidarity before beginning his prophetic work as described in Ezekiel 3:17.

questions.question: What title and responsibility does God give Ezekiel in Ezekiel 3:17?
options: Watchman unto the house of Israel, to hear God's word and give warning
High priest of Israel, to offer sacrifices
King over Israel, to lead them
questions.correctAnswer: Watchman unto the house of Israel, to hear God's word and give warning
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:17 explicitly calls Ezekiel a watchman for Israel, charged to hear God's words and warn the people, establishing his prophetic duty to alert them to danger, which is expanded in verses 18-21.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 3:18, what happens if Ezekiel does not warn the wicked of their ways?
options: The wicked shall die in their iniquity, and their blood will be required at Ezekiel's hand
The wicked will be forgiven anyway
The wicked will be immediately saved
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked shall die in their iniquity, and their blood will be required at Ezekiel's hand
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:18 states that if Ezekiel fails to warn the wicked, they will die for their sins and God will hold Ezekiel accountable for their blood, emphasizing the seriousness of his prophetic responsibility, which complements the warning role defined in verse 17.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 3:19 say will happen if Ezekiel warns the wicked but they do not turn from their ways?
options: The wicked will still die, but Ezekiel will have saved his own soul
The wicked will be forgiven because of Ezekiel's warning
Ezekiel will be punished for their stubbornness
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked will still die, but Ezekiel will have saved his own soul
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:19 clarifies that even if the wicked do not repent after being warned, they will die in their iniquity, but Ezekiel will have done his duty and saved his soul, highlighting personal responsibility in obedience to God's command, as introduced in verses 17-18.

questions.question: Based on Ezekiel 3:20, what consequence does a righteous man face if he turns from righteousness and Ezekiel does not warn him?
options: He shall die in his sin, and his past righteousness will not be remembered
He will be forgiven without consequence
He will be punished but his righteousness will be remembered
questions.correctAnswer: He shall die in his sin, and his past righteousness will not be remembered
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:20 teaches that if a righteous person turns to sin and is not warned, he will die in sin and lose the memory of his previous righteousness, and Ezekiel will be held accountable, emphasizing the importance of warning both wicked and righteous (see also verses 17-19).

questions.question: What promise is given in Ezekiel 3:21 if Ezekiel warns the righteous man and he does not sin?
options: The righteous man shall surely live, and Ezekiel has delivered his soul
The righteous man will still die
The righteous man will be judged harshly
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous man shall surely live, and Ezekiel has delivered his soul
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:21 promises that if the righteous is warned and does not sin, he will live, and Ezekiel will have delivered his own soul, reinforcing the value of obedience and the prophet's role in saving lives through warning, as established in earlier verses of this section.

questions.question: What command does God give Ezekiel in Ezekiel 3:22?
options: Arise, go forth into the plain, and God will talk with him there
Build an altar by the river
questions.correctAnswer: Arise, go forth into the plain, and God will talk with him there
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:22 records God's command for Ezekiel to arise and go into the plain where God will speak with him, continuing the intimate communication between God and Ezekiel, following his initial prophetic instructions.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel respond in Ezekiel 3:23 when he sees the glory of the LORD in the plain?
options: He sings a song of praise
questions.correctAnswer: He falls on his face
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:23 describes Ezekiel falling on his face upon seeing the glory of the LORD, showing reverence and awe, consistent with his prophetic experience and submission to God's presence.

questions.question: What instruction is given to Ezekiel in Ezekiel 3:24 regarding his conduct?
options: Go, shut thyself within thine house
Go and prophesy openly in the city
Build a school for the children
questions.correctAnswer: Go, shut thyself within thine house
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:24 commands Ezekiel to shut himself within his house, indicating a period of confinement or symbolic isolation, which is further explained in the following verses about being bound and silent among the rebellious house.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 3:26, God will make Ezekiel's tongue cleave to the roof of his mouth so that he cannot speak to the rebellious house.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:26 states that God will make Ezekiel's tongue cleave to the roof of his mouth, rendering him silent and unable to rebuke the rebellious house, illustrating a period of enforced silence.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 3:27 promises that when God speaks to Ezekiel, his mouth will be opened to deliver God's message to the rebellious house.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:27 assures that God will open Ezekiel's mouth when He chooses, enabling him to speak God's words to the rebellious house, highlighting divine control over prophetic speech.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 3.

questions.question: What responsibility is given to Ezekiel as a watchman over the house of Israel?
options: To warn the wicked to turn from their ways
To offer sacrifices for the people
questions.correctAnswer: To warn the wicked to turn from their ways
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:17 states that Ezekiel is made a watchman to warn the house of Israel, which includes warning the wicked about their ways.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 3:18, what happens if the watchman does not warn the wicked man?
options: The wicked man shall die in his iniquity and his blood will be required at the watchman’s hand
The wicked man will be forgiven
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked man shall die in his iniquity and his blood will be required at the watchman’s hand
questions.explanation: Verse 18 clearly states that if the watchman does not warn the wicked, the wicked will die in his sin, and the watchman will be held accountable for his blood.

questions.question: What is the consequence described in Ezekiel 3:20 when a righteous man turns to sin and the watchman fails to warn him?
options: The man will die in his sin, and his previous righteousness will not be remembered
The man will be forgiven automatically
The watchman is praised for discretion
questions.correctAnswer: The man will die in his sin, and his previous righteousness will not be remembered
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:20 explains that if the righteous man turns to sin and is not warned, he will die in his sin and lose the remembrance of his past righteousness.

questions.question: What happens if the watchman warns the righteous man and he does not sin, according to Ezekiel 3:21?
options: He shall surely live and the watchman has delivered his soul
He will be punished for past sins
questions.correctAnswer: He shall surely live and the watchman has delivered his soul
questions.explanation: Verse 21 states that when the righteous man is warned and does not sin, he will live and the watchman saves himself by giving the warning.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 3:22-23, what did Ezekiel do when the glory of the LORD appeared to him in the plain?
questions.correctAnswer: He fell on his face
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:23 records that when the glory of the LORD stood before him as by the river of Chebar, Ezekiel fell on his face in reverence.

questions.question: What command did the spirit give Ezekiel in Ezekiel 3:24?
options: Go, shut thyself within thine house
questions.correctAnswer: Go, shut thyself within thine house
questions.explanation: Verse 24 states that the spirit entered Ezekiel and commanded him to shut himself within his house.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 3:25-26, what will happen to Ezekiel that will affect his ability to speak to the people?
options: He will be bound and made dumb so he cannot speak except when God opens his mouth
He will be given a loud voice to rebuke the people
He will be sent to another nation
questions.correctAnswer: He will be bound and made dumb so he cannot speak except when God opens his mouth
questions.explanation: Verses 25-26 describe that Ezekiel will be bound and his tongue made to cleave to the roof of his mouth, rendering him dumb until God commands him to speak.

questions.question: What is the repeated phrase used in Ezekiel 3:27 to describe the people Ezekiel is to address?
questions.correctAnswer: They are a rebellious house
questions.explanation: Verse 27 ends with the phrase 'for they are a rebellious house,' emphasizing the stubbornness of the people Ezekiel is to address.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'watchman' in Ezekiel 3:17 most closely means:
options: Sentinel or guard who watches for danger
questions.correctAnswer: Sentinel or guard who watches for danger
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'tsaphah' used for 'watchman' implies a sentinel or guard whose duty is to watch and warn of approaching danger, fitting Ezekiel's role here.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected to Ezekiel's role as a watchman warning the wicked?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 62:6
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:6 also speaks of watchmen who never keep silent, guarding Jerusalem and warning the people, paralleling Ezekiel's watchman role (Ezekiel 3:17).

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Ezekiel 3:18-21 where contrasting outcomes for wicked and righteous are presented?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The passage uses parallelism, contrasting the fate of the wicked and the righteous based on whether they are warned or not, a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel’s experience in Ezekiel 3:14 (going in bitterness and heat of spirit) relate to the prophetic call experience in Isaiah 6?
options: Both prophets experience overwhelming divine presence resulting in emotional intensity
Only Ezekiel experiences bitterness, Isaiah does not
Isaiah was joyful, Ezekiel was bitter
questions.correctAnswer: Both prophets experience overwhelming divine presence resulting in emotional intensity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:14 describes a strong emotional reaction to God’s call, similar to Isaiah 6 where Isaiah is moved deeply by God’s holiness, showing a shared prophetic call pattern.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel was sent to speak to people who spoke a strange language and hard speech that he could not understand.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:5-6 explicitly states he was sent to the house of Israel, not to many people of strange speech and hard language he could not understand.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel's forehead is described as being made harder than flint to withstand the rebellious house's opposition.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:8-9 states that God made Ezekiel's face and forehead strong and as hard as adamant, harder than flint, so he would not fear the rebellious people's opposition.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of Ezekiel's responsibility to warn others as seen in Ezekiel 3:17-21?
questions.correctAnswer: James 5:19-20
questions.explanation: James 5:19-20 speaks of turning a sinner from the error of his way to save his soul from death, reflecting Ezekiel’s watchman duty to warn and save others (Ezekiel 3:19-21).

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 3:1-3 symbolically suggest about the prophet's reception of God's message?
options: The message is bitter and difficult to accept
The message is sweet and nourishing like honey
The message is irrelevant to Israel
The message is secret and must be hidden
questions.correctAnswer: The message is sweet and nourishing like honey
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:3 states that the roll he ate was 'in my mouth as honey for sweetness,' symbolizing that God's word, though heavy in responsibility, is delightful and spiritually nourishing.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 3:5-6, why was Ezekiel not sent to foreigners but specifically to the house of Israel?
options: Because Israel was more rebellious than other nations
Because Israel spoke the same language and could understand him
Because Israel was the only nation under God's covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Because Israel spoke the same language and could understand him
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:5 explains that Ezekiel was not sent to a people with a strange speech and hard language but to the house of Israel, implying that communication and understanding were possible within Israel.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated in Ezekiel 3:8-9 where God makes Ezekiel's face 'strong against their faces' and his forehead 'as an adamant harder than flint'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty and empowerment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:8-9 reveals God's sovereign power to strengthen Ezekiel to endure opposition, showing divine empowerment to fulfill a difficult prophetic role.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 3:11, what does God command Ezekiel to do despite the people's potential refusal to listen?
options: To speak God's words regardless of their response
To leave them and find a new audience
To perform miracles to force their belief
questions.correctAnswer: To speak God's words regardless of their response
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:11 instructs Ezekiel to deliver God's message to the exiles whether they will hear or forbear, emphasizing the duty to proclaim the word regardless of acceptance.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 3:12-13 describe the manifestation of God's glory that Ezekiel experiences?
options: A great rushing sound with noises of wings and wheels
A bright fire consuming the earth
A gentle whisper in the wind
questions.correctAnswer: A great rushing sound with noises of wings and wheels
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:12-13 details Ezekiel hearing a great rushing sound, the noise of wings of living creatures touching, and the noise of wheels, symbolizing the overwhelming presence and glory of God.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is highlighted in Ezekiel 3:17-19 regarding Ezekiel's role as a watchman?
options: The doctrine of human responsibility and corporate accountability
The doctrine of salvation by works
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of human responsibility and corporate accountability
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:17-19 teaches that Ezekiel, as a watchman, is responsible to warn the wicked; failure to warn results in culpability, emphasizing human responsibility and accountability in divine judgment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 3:20-21, what is the outcome if a righteous person is warned and does not sin?
options: They will be forgotten by God
They shall surely live and Ezekiel delivers his soul
They will still be punished for past sins
questions.correctAnswer: They shall surely live and Ezekiel delivers his soul
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:21 states that if the righteous man is warned and refrains from sin, he will live, and Ezekiel is delivered from responsibility for that person's death.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 3:25-26 teach about God's control over the prophet's ability to speak to the rebellious house?
options: Ezekiel will freely travel and preach as he wishes
God will silence Ezekiel until He chooses to speak
Ezekiel will perform miracles to convince the people
Ezekiel's message will be accepted without resistance
questions.correctAnswer: God will silence Ezekiel until He chooses to speak
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:25-26 shows that God will bind Ezekiel and cause his tongue to cleave to the roof of his mouth, making him silent until God commands him to speak, demonstrating divine control over prophetic revelation.

questions.question: What does the combined teaching of Ezekiel 3:7 and 3:27 reveal about the nature of Israel's rebellion and God's patience?
options: Israel is quick to obey and God has no patience
Israel is rebellious and God allows selective hearing
Israel is rebellious, yet God persistently sends His word despite their rejection
Israel is faithful and God rewards their obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Israel is rebellious, yet God persistently sends His word despite their rejection
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:7 calls Israel 'impudent and hardhearted,' and 3:27 shows God commanding Ezekiel to speak to them regardless of their response, highlighting God's persistent patience and desire for repentance despite rebellion.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 3:22-23 reveal about the prophet's encounter with God's glory and its significance to his prophetic mission?
options: Ezekiel experiences God's glory as a sign of judgment to come
Ezekiel witnesses God's glory as a reassurance and commissioning for his mission
Ezekiel sees God's glory and immediately flees in fear
Ezekiel ignores the glory and focuses on the people
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel witnesses God's glory as a reassurance and commissioning for his mission
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:22-23 describes the glory of the LORD standing before Ezekiel, similar to earlier visions, signifying divine presence and empowering him to fulfill his prophetic duties.

questions.question: How do Ezekiel 3:1 and 3:17 together inform the doctrine of prophetic responsibility in the Old Testament?
options: Prophets only speak when the people ask
Prophets are passive receivers of visions without active duties
Prophets must ingest God's word and then actively warn the people as watchmen
Prophets' warnings are optional and without consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets must ingest God's word and then actively warn the people as watchmen
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:1 commands Ezekiel to eat the roll (receive God's word), and 3:17 appoints him as a watchman to warn Israel, showing the active responsibility of prophets to internalize and proclaim God's message.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that prophetic warnings are meaningless if the audience is rebellious and refuses to listen. What does Ezekiel 3:11 and 3:27 teach about the purpose of the prophetic message?
options: The message is only for those who already believe
Prophets should stop speaking if the people refuse to listen
Prophetic messages must be delivered regardless of acceptance to fulfill God's justice
The prophet can ignore the rebellious and focus elsewhere
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic messages must be delivered regardless of acceptance to fulfill God's justice
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:11 commands Ezekiel to speak whether the people hear or forbear, and 3:27 reiterates that the prophet speaks 'Thus saith the Lord GOD,' regardless of response, showing the necessity of proclamation for divine justice.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Ezekiel 3:18-19 and 3:20-21 provide about divine justice and human warning?
options: Warning others removes personal responsibility for their judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Warning others removes personal responsibility for their judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:18-19 and 3:20-21 make clear that if the prophet warns the wicked or the righteous, he is delivered from their blood; human responsibility includes warning others, and God's justice accounts for this.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is especially emphasized in Ezekiel 3:14 where 'the hand of the LORD was strong upon me' during Ezekiel's bitterness and spiritual heat?
questions.correctAnswer: God's sustaining power
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:14 shows God's strong hand upon Ezekiel, sustaining him through bitterness and spiritual struggle, emphasizing God's power to uphold His servants.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 3:15's detail of Ezekiel sitting among the captives 'astonished' for seven days contribute to understanding the prophet's role in redemptive history?
options: It shows Ezekiel's rejection by the people
It symbolizes the period of reflection and identification with Israel's suffering
It indicates Ezekiel's failure as a prophet
It marks a time of divine silence
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the period of reflection and identification with Israel's suffering
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:15 portrays Ezekiel seated among the captives in astonishment for seven days, illustrating his deep identification with Israel's exile and the prophet's role as mediator in redemptive history.
